newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel approves budget accord with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel approves budget accord with Clinton.

text.p: The Senate Budget Committee Monday approved the fiscal 1998 budget resolution that embodies the balanced-budget accord reached between the White House and congressional leaders last week.
The full Senate and House will consider the budget plan Tuesday. The measure cleared the panel on a bipartisan vote of 17-4. It had cleared the House panel last Friday.

The budget cleared the committee without any significant changes to the agreement reached with the White House. However, several amendments which failed in the committee will be brought before the full Senate.

The agreement reins in federal spending for some domestic programs such as Medicare, the health care program for the elderly, in an attempt to bring the federal budget to balance over the next five years. It also provides U.S. President Bill Clinton with more money for education and the environment.

It also provides a net tax cut of $85 billion through 2002 aimed at giving families tax breaks for education and children, cutting capital gains tax rates, expansion of individual retirement accounts and lowering inheritance taxes.

The accord has been praised by Clinton and many of his Democrats as well as Republicans as an attempt to ease political strife over government spending. This year's deficit is expected to total $67 billion, well below the nearly $300 billion of the early 1990s. Political battles in the next few months over the legislation needed to enact the savings and tax cuts are expected to be long and difficult.
